description: Real-world source fixtures fetched via curl from raw.githubusercontent.com from well-known open-source projects. Used to prove the UniversalEngine against real online code and to keep future tests hermetic (no network needed at test time).

files.expectedBehavior: Detected as Go CLI/command domain; routed to native `go run`. NOTE: this real file imports golang.org/x/example/hello/reverse, an external module that is not part of the file, so compilation inside the engine's synthetic module is expected to fail with a missing-module error (honest negative result).
Self-contained Go program (imports only fmt); native-run route; prints `Hello, 世界` and exits 0.

Self-contained ES module util (linear search); native-run route with node; the module loads cleanly and exits 0 with no stdout (the file only defines and exports functions; its demo calls are commented out upstream).

Self-contained Java class with a main method implementing the Luhn checksum; declares `package com.thealgorithms.others;`. The engine places the source at <workdir>/com/thealgorithms/others/Luhn.java (package-aware placement) and runs the fully-qualified class on the JVM; the Luhn usage examples print to stdout. Verified by tests/real-world.test.ts.

files.project: TheAlgorithms/Java (historical revision 8c78d90, 2017, before the package restructure)
files.expectedBehavior: Self-contained Java file with a main method (no package declaration); native-run route via JDK single-file source mode; sorts {170, 45, 75, 90, 802, 24, 2, 66} and prints the sorted numbers.

Real Rust intro exercise printing a Rustlings ASCII banner via println!, including r#"..."# raw strings. No rustc on this machine, so the engine routes transpile-then-run through the structural rust->go converter (raw strings are converted to Go quoted strings; leaked Rust-isms are reported in structuralReport.unsupported) and executes the output with Go, printing the real Rustlings banner. Verified by tests/real-world.test.ts.

Real Haskell module with a main = do block implementing bubble sort with where-clauses and pattern matching; no ghc on this machine, so the engine must route transpile-then-run via the structural haskell->javascript converter and run the output with node; guards/where/multiple-equation functions are beyond the simple structural converter, so partial conversion is expected (structuralReport.converted/unsupported tells the truth).
